study.title: Psalm 55: anguish, betrayal, and ultimate trust in God
study.overview: This psalm is an intense prayer of someone afflicted by enemies and, especially painfully, by a friend who became a traitor. The psalmist begins by asking God to hear his cry, describes the deep fear that dominates him and expresses the desire to escape violence. Afterwards, he denounces the corruption he sees around and laments the wound caused by the betrayal of someone very close. In the second half, he reaffirms that he will continue crying out to the Lord, declares confidence that God will hear him and conclude by handing over the destiny of the wicked to God, while he decides to remain trusting in the Lord.

outline.title: Clamor for Divine Attention
outline.explanation: The psalmist asks that God does not hide and describes the pressure of enemies and the intensity of his pain. Suffering is presented as something urgent, not abstract: there is oppression, threat and cry for response.

outline.title: Extreme angle and desire to escape
outline.explanation: The crisis already reaches the interior of the psalmist: fear, trembling and horror consumes it. He imagines running away as a dove to escape the wind and the storm, an image that shows the unbearable weight of the situation.

outline.title: Violence in the city and betrayal of a friend
outline.explanation: The psalmist calls for judgment against the violence and falsehood present in the city. Pain deepens because the aggressor is not an open enemy, but a fellow trust, someone of his coexistence and his counsel, whose betrayal makes the blow more serious.

outline.title: Perseverance in prayer and trust in God's judgment
outline.explanation: Despite the crisis, the psalmist decides to continue calling upon God in constant prayer. He believes that the Lord will save him, humiliate the wicked, and judge the violent and deceivers, while he himself concludes by affirming confidence in God.

study.context: The notes provided indicate that many interpreters associate the psalm with the crisis caused by a nearby enemy, possibly linked to a rebellion and betrayal of a former friend. However, this appears as an interpretative conjecture, not as an indisputable data of the text. The psalm itself emphasizes the contrast between the violence of the adversaries and the fidelity of God, without requiring us to identify with historical certainty all the characters.
study.theology: The psalm teaches that biblical faith does not deny pain, but takes it before God in prayer. Suffering here includes real fear, impossible escape sensation and the deep wound caused by the betrayal of someone close. Theologically, the text shows three important movements. First, God is the trustworthy listener when human justice fails. Second, wickedness is not overlooked: the Lord judges violence, falsehood and breaking of covenant. Third, the answer of the righteous is not only to ask for vengeance, but to continue trusting in God and giving Him the weight. The notes also allow a typological Christian reading: the betrayal of a friend analogously recalls the suffering of Jesus, although the very psalm does not make this application directly. The moral conclusion of the text is that trust in God remains even when visible signs seem to favor the wicked.

scholarViews.insight: The psalm ends by showing that dying early means not fully experiencing the blessing of God, which reinforces judgment on bloodthirsty and deceiving men.
The psalmist's pain is aggravated because the aggressor was rather a close friend, and not just a declared enemy.
The reference to pray in the afternoon, in the morning and at noon is presented as the usual practice of the pious Hebrews, highlighting perseverance in prayer.

questions: How does the psalmist teach us to transform fear and pain into honest prayer before God?
Why does the betrayal of a friend so deep, and how does the psalm deal with this wound without denying divine justice?
How does the decision to trust God, even before seeing the answer, confronts our tendency to seek immediate exits?
study.practice: Take to God, in specific prayer, what causes you today fear, injustice or disappointment. If there is betrayal or relational conflict, not only does bitterness feed: give the case to the Lord and continue to practice trust through constant prayer. It is also worth observing the discipline of the psalm: repeated, sincere and persevering prayer throughout the day. Instead of reacting only with impulse, ask God to preserve his heart and do justice in his time.
study.uncertainty: There is historical uncertainty as to the exact scenario of the psalm and the identity of the characters behind the betrayal; the notes present this as conjecture, not as sure. It is also necessary to distinguish between Christian application to the suffering of Jesus and the direct meaning of the psalm, which speaks first of David's experience/ the psalmist. In addition, some notes in English suggest theological and liturgical details that are interpretations, not explicit statements of the biblical text.
